text:
maya: Heads up — vendor sent a critical PDU firmware patch that requires staggered power cycles for racks in us-west1. Target window: Tue 2026-03-24 01:00–03:00 UTC. We need a drain + fallback plan for affected racks (rack-7, rack-8).

devin: Ack. Are we doing full node power cycles or per-PDU outlets?

maya: Per-PDU (affects half the rack at a time). Expected ~5–7 min for each PDU cycle, but we'll schedule 15min per PDU to be safe and validate.

lina: Request: freeze non-critical infra deploys for the window? Any long-running jobs we should preemptively reschedule?

ron: Agree on freeze. Also need to ensure Dedicated customers with pinned capacity are not impacted — we'll route traffic off the racks first.

devin: Capacity check: current free GPU headroom in us-west1 is ~18% (mostly spread across other racks). Bulk batch queue has 320 waiting jobs; avg job uses 1 GPU. If we drain both racks concurrently we'll lose ~42 GPUs. Plan: do one rack at a time and bump scheduling affinity to prefer other racks.

maya: Plan draft:
- Pre-window: 00:30 UTC — set cluster-scheduler soft-affinity to prefer us-west1-other-racks (will take a few minutes).
- 00:40 UTC — send customer and internal notices, freeze deploys.
- 01:00 UTC — start rack-7 PDU1 cycle: cordon + drain nodes -> wait for pods to land.
- 01:20 UTC — PDU2 cycle for rack-7.
- 01:40 UTC — validate, give 10m buffer, then start rack-8 at 01:55.
- Finish by 03:00 UTC.

devin: For drains use:```
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='app!=stateful' --timeout=10m
```
We'll skip force unless absolutely needed. Add to runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/pdu-powercycle

ron: How do we handle stateful workloads (DBs / long GPUs)? Any affinity pinned to those racks?

lina: Checked: 2 stateful GPU jobs pinned to rack-7 via nodeAffinity (ml-workloads namespace). I can ask owners to checkpoint or we can migrate via snapshot + restart — prefer owners to handle. Paging @ml-platform owners now.

ops-oncall: I'll be on standby for the window. If drain stalls >12m escalate to me. I can also throttle the PDU cycle if pods don't evacuate.

maya: Good. Reminder to add rollback instructions: if PDU cycle causes unexpected node failures, we will: 1) stop further cycles, 2) power-on failed outlets, 3) mark nodes unschedulable and rebuild.

k8s-bot: Automated check: cluster has 42 nodes in rack-7/8. Current nodeReady=false count is 1. Suggest running `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector=status.phase!=Running` after each drain.

devin: Cost note: If we redirect jobs to GPU spots in other regions briefly, cross-region egress for logs could spike cost by ~$120/hour. Should we allow temporary cross-region bursting or keep within region?

ron: Keep within region if possible. Ops budget approved a $1k contingency for emergency bursts this quarter, but prefer to avoid extra egress.

maya: Final asks:
- @lina please send the external customer notification and add a hold on new Dedicated provisioning for us-west1 during window.
- @devin run the pre-window capacity test at 00:45 UTC and post results here.
- @ron coordinate with account team for any high-priority customers.
- I'll own the runbook updates and postmortem template.

lina: Will do. Draft sent to #customer-notify for review, will post in 10m.

devin: Pre-window capacity test results (00:46): available GPUs after soft-affinity bump = 38, batch queue trimmed to 240 after auto-cancel of short-idle jobs. We should be safe to do single-rack at a time.

ops-oncall: Oncall note: I enabled extended retries for KV-cache writes during drains to reduce warmup errors.

maya: Thanks team. We'll start the posted steps at 00:30. Will update thread with live timeline during the window. :white_check_mark:
